body:
Found while reviewing PR #881. #897 is one instance; this is the backlog.

`MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` §3 step 2 requires the following for a hydrate with no exact ontology term:
- its own identity (`cas:` or `kgmicrobe.compound:`);
- a `skos:broadMatch` to the nearest parent;
- the Rule B1 registry row.

The #245 ruling rejected `closeMatch` here, and #664 moved four sulfate hydrates off it. Among MAPPED records whose preferred term states a hydrate, counted on #881's head:

| identity | mapping_quality → parent predicate | records |
|---|---|---:|
| `cas:` | CLOSE_MATCH → `skos:closeMatch` | 45 (one is `Mgso4h2o`, fixed by #881) |
| `kgmicrobe.compound:` | CLOSE_MATCH → `skos:closeMatch` | 28 |
| `cas:` | NARROW_MATCH → `skos:broadMatch` | 12 |
| `kgmicrobe.compound:` | NARROW_MATCH → `skos:broadMatch` | 7 |

Examples:
- `cas:` with closeMatch: `Sodium_Deoxycholate_Monohydrate`, `L-Glutamic_Acid_Monopotassium_Salt_Monohydrate`, `Fosmidomycin_Sodium_Salt_Hydrate`;
- `kgmicrobe.compound:` with closeMatch: `Cocl2_X_4_H2o`, `Na2hpo4_X_3_H2o`, `Fecl2_X_6_H2o`, `Fecl2_X_7_H2o`, `Cu_No32_X_3_H2o`.

**Why it matters:**
- kg-microbe's consolidator treats `closeMatch` as symmetric (`scripts/consolidate_chemical_mappings.py:1776`, 1829-1873 at 1acb8b61f). It merges the hydrate's label and `other` tokens into the anhydrous parent's record and force-sets the parent's `canonical_name` to the hydrate label; the last row written wins.
- This comes from reading the code. I did not run kg-microbe or check which of these parents it actually renames.

**Also:**
- `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` (§3 step 2) says 34 hydrate subjects carry the broadMatch pattern. The count above is lower, so the doc or the data has drifted.
- `Cu_No32_X_3_H2o` keeps a local identity although its own CAS, 10031-43-3 (copper(II) nitrate trihydrate), is on the record. §3 step 2 would make it `cas:10031-43-3`.

**Related:** #696 (BROAD_MATCH publishes closeMatch) and #884 (schema direction of NARROW/BROAD).

**Fix:** a reviewed batch moving these records to NARROW_MATCH, with broadMatch and registry rows through the receipt chain. Check first which of them are SUPPORTED, because changing the bytes cancels approvals (#898).

## History

**How the cohort got here:**
- #342 (`scripts/regrade_hydrate_to_close_match.py`, in #500 on 2026-08-28) regraded 72 hydrate→anhydrous rows from narrowMatch to closeMatch on purpose. Its reason: narrowMatch claims a subsumption that ChEBI contradicts.
- That script also took those records out of Rule B1's scope.
- 72 SSSOM rows still carry `MIM:curator=regrade_hydrate_to_close_match`.

**The later ruling:**
- The #245 ruling (#735, 2026-09-22) settled the subsumption concern differently. It keeps `skos:broadMatch`, reads it as "form of", and forbids projecting it as `subclass_of`.
- It also records that `closeMatch` was rejected because it carries no direction and drops Rule B1.
- §3 step 2 has required broadMatch plus the registry row since then.
- #664 moved four sulfate hydrates back to that shape.

**Decision for maintainers:** these 73 are the #342 cohort the ruling did not migrate, so whether to migrate them is a maintainer decision, not a data error introduced by one PR.

Reconciled this cohort against main `4625afd492b6cf43e3b499d1425d2453d490009d` and the current full file/decision scopes of open PRs #912 and #914 before applying any correction.

The current mapped CAS/local hydrate selection has 72 CLOSE_MATCH records, rather than the historical 73 in this issue title. PR #912 owns 68 of those records. Two further records, FeCl2 x 7 H2O and 2-keto-D-gluconic acid hemicalcium salt monohydrate, intersect PR #914's scientific rejection ledger and remain outside this batch. Shared aggregate filenames were not treated as scientific overlap.

Current MAPPING_SEMANTICS section 3 and the settled form-of ruling support a bounded correction for D-(+)-melezitose monohydrate: preserve `cas:10030-67-8` as the distinct supplied-form identity and `CHEBI:6731` as its parent; replace CLOSE_MATCH with NARROW_MATCH, exported as `skos:broadMatch`, and supply the required B1 local identity row. Live [PubChem CID 16217716](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16217716) agrees with the existing monohydrate formula and stereochemical InChI. Parent [CID 92817](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/92817) agrees with [CHEBI:6731](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:6731). Exact hydrate name/CAS searches found no hydrate ChEBI term in current OLS and the pinned local database. CHEBI:183824 is anhydrous and stereochemically different, so it is not an alternative exact hydrate identity. No record merge, role approval or identifier replacement is proposed.

Sodium perchlorate monohydrate also has source-supported form/parent evidence, but its approved cellular-role plan pins the complete YAML record. The current native builder refuses a mapping edit to those bytes. Its correction is therefore deferred to the explicit approval-free supersession mechanism in PR #764; that guard will not be waived or duplicated.

I will apply only the melezitose parent correction through the guarded writer, preserve historical evidence, generate the scoped SSSOM rows, and record an approval-free mapping-change receipt. The provisional carbon role remains open, and the old CAS mapping approval must not carry automatically across changed source bytes. Native reviewed-release and semantic checks plus independent review are required before publication. This bounded change does not resolve the remaining cohort or close this issue. No paid provider calls were used.

The native publication attempt identified a second approval-pin dependency on PR #764. The guarded melezitose correction and scoped generated rows were prepared, but the current completion assembler rejects the old positive CAS mapping cohort because its source record changed: `Nonmapping-cohort approval has stale owner or row` (frozen cohort row 931, current canonical row 919). An approval-free mapping-change receipt does not currently supersede that pin.

The failure and complete unpublished proposal are preserved as evidence. The existing approval will not be rewritten or bypassed. The melezitose source and canonical rows are being restored to their verified original bytes, and this issue remains open; no melezitose correction is being published in this batch. Sodium perchlorate monohydrate remains deferred for its separate whole-record approved-role pin. Both scientifically supported form/parent corrections should be applied after PR #764 provides the native supersession path and then receive fresh mapping-specific review.

The expanded exact-term search also found no exact melezitose monohydrate term through current OLS all-ontology name/CAS queries or NCIT CAS lookup. Broad NCIT melezitose results were microbial organism descriptions, not chemical identities. This remains bounded negative evidence, not a claim about all possible ontology releases.

PRs #912 and #914 retain their existing scientific scopes. This batch continues only with the independently verified #669/#1003 alias corrections that do not require changing the blocked source records or overriding review pins. No scientific/release approval is inferred from passing structural checks.

[PR #1007](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/pull/1007) preserves the melezitose proposal and exact native failure, but ships no melezitose or sodium-perchlorate record changes. The melezitose source and mapping rows were restored exactly after the current assembler refused to supersede its frozen SUPPORTED CAS cohort; sodium also has a whole-record role approval pin. Both require PR #764 rather than weakened guards or edited old approvals. The cohort/PR #912/#914 boundaries and source-supported form-of recommendation are documented in [the audit and blocked scientific review](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/blob/bf7d514c804670ea3db3e9e75a2c94624554fa26/reports/sssom_scientific_curation_20261101/README.md). The safe alias-only remainder passes native checks and independent re-review. This issue remains open.

The strict receipt port has merged in #1068 as `e568dbf0e0f759431ed317b973675680f031dd1d`, with all PR and merge-group checks passing and no scientific approvals added. The approved plan now continues with D-(+)-melezitose monohydrate on a fresh isolated branch from that main.

Retain `cas:10030-67-8`, CHEBI:6731, the existing chemistry, empty synonym list, source occurrences and provisional carbon role. Change CLOSE_MATCH to NARROW_MATCH/broadMatch under the settled form-of rule, add the native B1 handle, preserve the #342 history, and record an approval-free receipt. The separate generic hydrate remains untouched. The old CAS support must first withdraw; only a fresh mapping-specific assessment of the actual corrected owner and generated parent/CAS/B1 rows can supply new support. #1070 tracks the bounded review-consumer capability.

The live #912 file inventory contains neither named monohydrate owner; its assembler overlap is only its historical source-hash anchor, not this review capability. Its remaining cohort and the 23 deferred alias pairs stay outside this correction. Sodium perchlorate follows in its own PR after the melezitose merge. This issue remains open for the wider cohort. No paid provider calls or role approvals are part of this correction.

The melezitose monohydrate correction is applied through the guarded writer and synchronized at local checkpoint `585b90b47d54cd110709d263ea1e754a47106654`. One owner changes: CLOSE_MATCH→NARROW_MATCH plus a new evidence/history event; CAS identity, chemistry, aliases, occurrences, provisional carbon role and old #342 history remain intact.

The merged `9bd09b2ba163212a65289b91313f98cb0937476f` producer candidate (2,975 rows) passed native invariants with zero rejects and an empty Rule K baseline. Available B4 ontology files were hash-bound and checked; BTO/MICRO transforms are unavailable. The guarded projection independently verifies exactly two replaced canonical rows plus one added B1 row, 2,979 unrelated rows and the complete header unchanged.

Source-token decision for this bounded PR: retain the current native producer vocabulary and commit the recovered upstream manifest evidence. The two existing rows replace eight historical `kgm:` tokens with `kgm:mediaingredientmech_reviewed[manifest=9bb29d5605d93dea351be9624d99c5d8ada57d4b9831b22764957b784bd685af]` and `kgm:native_ontology:chebi`; the added handle carries the same source cell. These are parent-entity loader provenance propagated by the producer, not current claim-specific scientific approval. The exact original manifest was recovered from artifact 10852467926 / workflow run 36109949250 and matches the committed KG pin; all three artifact product hashes and the historical source/review Git blobs at `1848b0fe521bc2462f165912fcf92d09ad9a8cec` were verified. The historical CAS approval will be withdrawn after the owner correction; fresh mapping-specific review must independently assess all three actual claims.

The parent row also removes the CAS token from `other` and clears the old validation stamp; the CAS row preserves its registry comment and validation stamp. All three rows carry the actual 2026-11-01 correction date. Full trace and recovered evidence are preserved under `reports/melezitose_form_901_20261101/upstream-provenance/` for the final PR.

#1070 adds the bounded review capability. Independent findings #1071, #1072 and #1073 were filed before repair and independently re-reviewed. Canonical promotion, receipt 20, fresh scientific assessment and final QC/PR remain the next steps; this comment grants no scientific approval.

The approved sequence continues after #1076 merged as `330d9e34c5cf69bb355d4d242977eb1a78dbe374`. Its melezitose correction, fresh mapping authority, CI portability fixes and branch cleanup are verified with 16 successful PR checks and 16 successful merge-group checks. This issue remains open for the remaining cohort.

The next isolated branch starts from that current main and covers only `Sodium_Perchlorate_Monohydrate.yaml`. Retain `cas:7791-07-3`, CHEBI:132103, its existing monohydrate chemistry, empty synonyms, occurrence counts and all historical evidence, including #342. [PubChem CID 516899](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/516899) lists the monohydrate CAS and ClH2NaO5/InChI matching the record; the inspected [ChEBI parent](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:132103) is sodium perchlorate. Under the settled section 3 form-of rule, change CLOSE_MATCH to NARROW_MATCH, publish the parent broadMatch and the required `kgmicrobe.compound:sodium_perchlorate_monohydrate` handle, and append an approval-free receipt through the strict #1068 path. The distinct anhydrous sodium-perchlorate record stays separate.

The existing ELECTRON_ACCEPTOR annotation, publication, organism/condition context and confidence remain intact. Its old release approval pins the complete owner bytes, so native supersession must withdraw that approval and reopen its finding. Fresh review will assess only the actual corrected mapping triplet; it will not renew the role approval. All melezitose authority, prior receipt prefixes and unrelated mapping decisions must remain intact.

The existing bounded searches have not resolved an exact eligible monohydrate grounding. SNOMED 765356005 remains an unverified alternative lead: its mirror label is preserved, primary concept access was blocked, and the current native ontology-source enum does not include SNOMED. This is neither a claim that the concept is absent nor permission to invent a registry workaround. The failed Sigma request likewise supplies no inspected supplier evidence. These limits will be retained in the fresh review.

The current full file inventories of all seven open PRs contain neither named monohydrate owner. #912 contains the distinct generic melezitose hydrate and shared generated/assembler surfaces; its remaining cohort and the 23 deferred alias pairs remain outside this correction. The isolated Claw producer is still current main `9bd09b2ba163212a65289b91313f98cb0937476f`. Native generation, receipt-chain checks, full QC, tests, independent adversarial review and the merge queue remain required. This decision comment grants no scientific approval; no paid provider calls are part of the work.

The preflight does not support a uniform CLOSE_MATCH-to-NARROW_MATCH conversion of the selected 67 owners. Six received primary source/form assessment; the other 61 received at most bounded cache candidate discovery. All three excluded identities remain outside the cohort.

After Step 7c merged as `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`, live main was rechecked at `2026-11-03T00:31:09.269512+00:00`. All 67 selected owner hashes and all 134 mapping decisions are unchanged: 125 WITHHOLD and nine SUPPORTED. Changing owner bytes must withdraw inherited support and require fresh claim-specific review. Complete current issue discussions and open-PR file inventories were reviewed; only #912 overlaps the selected owners. Independent deduplication supports two new focused findings: [#1117](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/1117) for the exact-term candidates and [#1118](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/1118) for G6501 chemistry. This preflight changes no source record or approval and supplies no new snapshot exception.

**Copper nitrate trihydrate:** the archived original source row, [PubChem CID 9837674](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/9837674) and [GSRS 066PG1506T](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/066PG1506T?view=full) agree on CAS 10031-43-3 and three waters. This independently supports the retained CAS; Step 7b's chemistry removal did not establish it. [ChEBI:78036](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chebi/CHEBI:78036) describes the water-free parent, CAS 3251-23-8, and owns the active `copper(2+) dinitrate` alias. Bounded local ChEBI/NCIt and upstream searches found no eligible exact trihydrate term. If that remains true at implementation, recommend the §3 own-CAS / broader-parent / B1 pattern, with a sourced rejection of the parent alias and preserved history. The missing anhydrous-name destination remains #900; this correction should not create an unrelated catalogue record. CAS CommonChemistry returned HTTP 401 and is not Registry verification.

**Sodium carbonate and D-maltose monohydrate:** locally resolved NCIT:C80911 and NCIT:C80300 have matching primary CAS/form evidence. Evaluate these exact candidates before the CAS-plus-parent fallback. The separate exact-term finding preserves the source evidence and maltose representation caveats. No identity or namespace has changed, and existing maltose role holds remain intact.

**Terpin hydrate:** source CAS 2451-01-6 and maintained prior evidence establish that `Terpene` denotes the intended terpin hydrate here, not the terpene class. CHEBI:751529 and NCIT:C219387 both resolve locally. ChEBI carries cis-related names but a structure without encoded stereochemistry; [GSRS S3V868548T](https://gsrs.ncats.nih.gov/api/v1/substances/S3V868548T?view=full) encodes cis-relative stereochemistry, and NCIt names that CAS/UNII. Establish whether the ChEBI concept denotes the exact supplied substance; if it is broader, consider the exact lower-priority ontology term. Otherwise preserve a distinct CAS identity with a qualified parent while the scope conflict stays open. Recommendation: resolve ChEBI's intended scope before choosing. Prefix priority does not establish exact substance equivalence.

**Ceftazidime hydrate:** the original catalogue is Sigma C3809. Sigma's deposited [PubChem SID 24892644](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/rest/pug/substance/sid/24892644/JSON) states that the product contains 10% sodium carbonate stabilizer. CHEBI:3509 denotes the pentahydrate, CAS 78439-06-2; the record/source uses CAS 120618-65-7 with unspecified hydration. That lexical candidate does not clear the NEEDS_SOURCE/semantic hold. The unresolved boundary is an active-hydrate identity with explicit formulation evidence versus the complete stabilized commercial material represented as a distinct mixture. Provisional recommendation: preserve the held active-hydrate owner and describe stabilized Sigma C3809 in `supplied_form`, pending confirmation that the owner denotes the active hydrate. Section 3 separates procurement detail from identity, and the supplier describes sodium carbonate as a stabilizer. If the source owner instead denotes the entire commercial preparation, a distinct mixture identity is required; the whole preparation must not inherit its active component's CAS or identity. Keep NEEDS_SOURCE/WITHHOLD. Neither option supports guessed hydration, pentahydrate approval, role approval or automatic merging.

**Glycerophosphate:** G6501 source and supplier/GSRS evidence establish an isomeric hydrate mixture. The current single water-free positional chemistry is unsupported for the whole source material. Correcting it is separable from deciding whether G6501 and the existing SUPPORTED `Sodium_glycerophosphate` owner of NCIT:C120561 denote the same mixture. Possible shared identity does not authorize merging, moving occurrences or inheriting approval. This concern differs from #1053's raw pentahydrate ambiguity and #1020's settled parent correction.

The unchanged native checker was independently rerun against actual main in a disposable fixture: baseline 21 passes; touching the complete selected cohort projects 77 against budget 25 and fails. The maintained snapshot and provenance remain unchanged. The [freshness constraint and exact proof](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/MediaIngredientMech/issues/894#issuecomment-6592153993) record why the approved single batch cannot proceed under the current snapshot prohibition. No Step 7d source implementation or promotion PR has started. The 23 deferred #669 alias pairs and #912 retirement remain later in the approved order.

The native scientific preflight is deliberately partial: six selected owners plus one adjacent owner received primary-source/form assessment. The other 61 have not received a full scientific review. Original captures, failed requests, native observations and the additive Ceftazidime wording review are preserved under `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7d-preflight/scientific-preflight/` and `step7c-independent/step7d-scientific-preflight-review/`; current-main readback and issue-dedup evidence are saved separately. No supervisor or cycle binding is introduced.

The user authorized a Step 7d-only unified snapshot rebuild, with every changed cell traced to this PR's reviewed owner edits or the existing 21-file main drift. That authorization supersedes the prior snapshot blocker for this PR only; the freshness budget, owner-selection rules, tests, evidence workflow and vendored pin remain protected.

A different explicit stop condition was confirmed before source edits. The current companion integration test hard-codes Step 7c's immutable companion path and requires it to match the release workflow. Step 7d's hash-changing canonical projection necessarily requires a new immutable companion successor. The existing native path therefore needs a test-selector update, which the latest instruction forbids. The evidence and narrow required authorization are recorded on #1105; #1013's prior decision already states that future refreshes require explicit selector updates. This is a prospective continuation incompatibility, not a current-main failing test or a defective stale-input safeguard.

Current main remains `467aa319a06ef992035f509f66fe251082b44ae1`. The exact current-selector test passes; an independent copied-input probe reproduces the expected stale companion refusal. No owner, aggregate, SSSOM, snapshot, test, workflow or pin has been edited. The isolated Step 7d branch has no commits beyond main and has not been pushed; no PR has been opened.

Priority #1117/#1118 assessment was stopped at the evidence gathered when this condition was confirmed. Its bounded observations are recorded on those issues and do not constitute the requested completed 67-owner scientific review. No include/drop batch or fresh scientific support is claimed. All three exclusions remain untouched. The subsequent 23 #669 alias pairs and #912 retirement remain pending in the approved order. #1109 stays open and its frozen helper remains unused.

Per the user's explicit stop rule, execution stops here. No paid research/provider calls, goal/cycle advancement, session restart or invented supervisor binding occurred. Evidence is retained under `output/approved-plan-20261101T031134Z/step7d-execution-20261103/`.

title: 73 hydrate records anchor their parent with closeMatch, which §3 step 2 rejects; kg-microbe folds them into the anhydrous parent
